speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're an adolescent with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. speaker: Doctor
text: That history of partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth is very specific; does your mother have a history of hirsutism or virilization, and have you been told you have "virilizing" features like deepening of the voice or increased muscle mass? REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous suggestion of Tuberculosis is incorrect given your history of congenital genital anomalies and bone fragility; those symptoms point toward a hormonal or genetic syndrome rather than an infection. While we await your 17-hydroxyprogesterone results, can you confirm if you have been told you have a "webbed neck" or "short stature," and do you recall having a single pigmented patch or "café-au-lait" spots on your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently taking oral isotretinoin for acne and an oral contraceptive. Social history: The patient is a high school student without significant tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency). The combination of ambiguous genitalia (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), severe acne, delayed menarche, and fractures due to osteoporosis from chronic cortisol/catecholamine excess is classic for this condition. The previous suggestion of tuberculosis is incorrect given the congenital anomalies.
